# Data source: Evaluated Nuclear Data File library (ENDF/B-VII.1; Chadwick et al. 2011)
# Nuclide selection originally from Hotokezaka et al. https://github.com/hotokezaka/HeatingRate
#
# Q, E_gamma, E_elec and meanlife are taken from the ENDF/B-VII.1 decay sublibrary, MF=8/MT=457.
# Q is the branching-ratio-weighted sum of the mode Q values, so it covers every decay branch of
# the nuclide including the beta-delayed neutron ones. E_gamma and E_elec are the tabulated
# average decay energies EEM (all electromagnetic radiation: gamma rays and X-rays) and ELP (all
# light particles: continuum betas plus conversion and Auger electrons), both averaged over one
# decay of the parent summed over its branches. They are not the averages of the tabulated
# spectra, which omit the X-ray and discrete-electron components and are absent altogether for
# the nuclides that ENDF evaluates from systematics.
# E_neutrino is the balance Q - EEM - ELP - EHP and is not read by ARTIS.
# One deviation from ENDF: Ta-188 uses the ENSDF half-life of 19.6(20) s rather than the 20 s
# ENDF rounds it to. ENDF assigns its parent Hf-188, which has no adopted ENSDF half-life, the
# same estimated 20 s, and two nuclides of one decay chain sharing a decay constant makes the
# Bateman solution singular.
# For a nuclide that alphadecays.txt gives a beta-minus branching ratio below one, E_elec is
# instead the average of the beta continuum alone, because the reader divides this column by that
# branching ratio and the discrete electrons of ELP are summed over all branches.
#
# A, Z, Q[MeV], E_gamma[MeV], E_elec[MeV], E_neutrino[MeV], meanlife[s]
